q: By the end of 2027, North Korea states explicitly in its official media that it has applied AI or automation technology to the Nuclear Trigger (the state's comprehensive nuclear weapons management system) or to its nuclear counterattack command system
basis: Announcements about delivery systems do not count (Kim Jong Un's February 2026 reference to AI in connection with the KN-25, which may have pointed to the production process, and May reports of an AI-guided cruise missile), nor does repetition of the law's wording that a strike is launched "automatically"; only an explicit statement that AI or automation technology has been applied to the command-and-control system counts. Nuclear powers have rarely stated officially that their nuclear command and control is technically automated (in 2011 the commander of Russia's Strategic Missile Forces confirmed that the Perimeter system exists and is on combat duty, but Moscow has never officially described how automated it is) · External variable X7 in the Korean Peninsula issue (shrinking human judgment and delegated authority)
